Imaging
[Hospital Day 5] CT head showed worsening of leftward subfalcine herniation with midline shift. From 9 mm --> 13 mm. Worsened obstructive dilatation of left ventricle with periventricular edema  No evidence of hemorrhagic conversion.

[Hospital Day 6] Status post expansion of the right hemicraniectomy as well as durotomy and placement of a drain. Slight improvement of midline shift, measuring 1.2 cm from 1.4 cm before. Persistent entrapment of the left lateral ventricle with ventriculomegaly and transependymal edema. Otherwise, no significant interval change.


 Assessment and Plan
[PATIENT NAME] is a 40 y.o.  with PMHx significant for prior stroke with residual L sided deficits presenting to ED on [Hospital Day 1] with L facial droop, L sided weakness, R gaze deviation and severe dysarthria, found to have loss of gray-white matter differentiation in R ACA-MCA territory and abrupt cut off of right ICA terminus. Patient not a candidate for intervention given level of stroke burden on CTH. Admitted to stroke team for continued workup, ICU level of care, with hospitalization complicated by worsening midline shift and progression of cerebral edema.
